The 2026 Texas gubernatorial election is scheduled to take place on November 3, 2026, to elect the governor of Texas. Republican incumbent Greg Abbott is seeking a fourth term.[1] He is being challenged by Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa.

Primary elections were held on March 3, 2026. Facing minimal opposition, Abbott won the Republican nomination with 82% of the vote. Hinojosa won the Democratic nomination with 59% of the vote over a field of candidates that included former Congressman Chris Bell.

If Abbott is re-elected and serves out his fourth term, he will become the state's longest-serving governor. Democrats have not won a gubernatorial election in Texas since 1990.

General election

[edit]

As of October 14, 2026[update], the candidates have not held a debate together, as Abbott has declined invitations from four separate Texas-based news outlets to debate Hinojosa.[65][66] If no debate is held it would mark the first gubernatorial election since 2010 that has not featured a debate between the two major party candidates.[67]

On the first day of early voting, Hinojosa announced that she was suing Abbott for allegedly violating the Texas Public Information Act by withholding certain email communications between Abbott and Elon Musk.[68][69]
